findings.F1: The day after a coin's largest falls (lowest tenth of the previous day's return over its 20-day volatility), the coin rose 0.56 % more than its normal daily drift (t 3.98, 1596 days), and 0.34 % more after the next tenth (t 2.82). Past the middle tenths the next day turns lower, down to -0.31 % in the eighth tenth (t -2.76). The next-day return falls as the previous day's standardised return grows in five of six coins: XMR t -5.23, ETH t -2.44, LTC t -2.25, BTC t -1.56. The move after the deepest falls is about 3 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip.
findings.F2: The tested forecast predicts only outside high volatility. Its 5-day slope has t 2.73 in the calmest third of 20-day volatility and t 2.56 in the middle third, with 1044 and 1043 cells. In the most volatile third it has t 0.18, and the cases with a positive forecast lost 0.62 % against the drift (485 cases). In the most volatile fifth, positive-forecast cells lost 1.12 % (281 cells).
findings.F3: The forecast's 5-day slope changes sign from year to year: t -1.34 in 2018, -2.17 in 2023, +2.35 in 2020, +2.35 in 2024 and +2.88 in 2025, with about 426 cells each. The confirmed effect does not hold steadily through time.
findings.F4: The book's gain rests on a few days. Its best 1 % of coin-days sum to 22.8 against a total of 15.0 over all coin-days, and its worst 1 % sum to -16.1.
findings.F5: Saturday is the one weekday whose daily return beats the drift in both halves of the data. Over all days it gained 0.29 % (t 3.40, 2280 days), with t 2.48 in <date> and t 2.40 in <date>. The book also earned most on Saturdays (0.25 %, t 5.37). Five of six coins show a positive Saturday, though none reaches t 2.1 alone, and a calendar effect cannot be graded, so it supports no idea here.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall over its last day, measured against its usual daily move over the past 20 days, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a coin after its sharpest one-day falls, sized by how unusual the fall was, and would refuse to sell into them.
ideas.name: sharp daily falls rebound

ideas.idea: When a coin's 20-day volatility is low against its own recent history, the larger its 28-day rise relative to its usual 28-day moves, the more the coin rises over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would ride a coin's strong month-long rises in calm markets and stand aside from them when the coin is turbulent.
ideas.name: calm monthly rises continue
